payload.goal: sofar list and sofar status report each initiative from the union of every copy of its log — each local worktree (uncommitted appends included), each local branch, each remote-tracking ref — and say which branch the progress lives on, so no checkout shows a stale or partial status. Read-only: never writes to another checkout's copy, never a new event type.

payload.text:
PROPOSAL, awaiting operator ruling (2026-09-21). No code yet.

PROBLEM, measured 2026-09-21. The record is committed on each branch, so every checkout folds only its own copy. SPEC §One launch directory per run (D6) already says so: "a plain worktree carries a stale COPY". It is worse than stale. The copies have FORKED: memory-lead's log has 11 event ids on main, 143 on r1-fixes, 132 on rust-core, 149 on wave-a and 143 on agents-parity. The union of all copies is 158 ids, and every copy is missing between 9 and 147 of them. So "go look at the branch" is wrong too. Other gaps: r1-fixes has 12 lines on main and 1886 on its branch; rust-core has 12 and 1080; agents-parity exists only on its own branch.

PROPOSED FIX: a read-side union fold. Per SPEC §Cursor primitive (sync-ready contract), the fold replays events in ulid order and import dedupes by id. Folding the union of all copies therefore gives exactly the state that merging every branch with merge=union would give. It is well defined, not a heuristic. Where the copies come from:
(1) Each `git worktree list --porcelain` entry: read its events.jsonl directly, so uncommitted appends count.
(2) Each local branch with no worktree, plus refs/remotes: one `git cat-file --batch` over `<ref>:.sofar/initiatives/<slug>/events.jsonl`.

DISPLAY: never show one silently merged number. Say where the progress lives, e.g. "32/43 · on r1-fixes (~/IO/sofar-r1-fixes), unmerged · main 0/18". A task done on a branch has not shipped to main, and an abandoned branch must not read as landed work.

HOOKS: the full union runs only in operator commands (list, status, the state server). SessionStart gets at most one cheap line, e.g. "N events of this record live on branch X". It is found by statting each worktree copy's size against the derived index, which keeps the hook inside the read-path perf budget.

FOLLOW-ON: a write guard. When this checkout's copy is behind another checkout's, warn: the decision is being made on stale state. Never redirect the write — writing into another checkout's copy forks its queue.

REJECTED:
(a) Moving the record off-branch (refs/sofar/* or the common git dir). The record would stop travelling with the code through PRs and merges, it overturns the committed-record premise that attribution, drift and shipwatch rest on, and it needs its own push refspec.
(b) Write-through, i.e. also appending every event to main's copy. It dirties main's tree under live peer sessions and duplicates lines at merge.
(c) "Merge more often". That is process, not product. The status stays stale between merges and is useless for WIP that cannot merge yet.
(d) Cloud sync alone. It covers other machines and has already shipped, but the free local engine must be honest on its own.

LIMIT: a teammate's unpushed branch on another machine is invisible to any local read. That case belongs to the sync client.

OPEN QUESTION for the operator: should remote-tracking refs count by default? They cover teammates' pushed branches, but they also drag in abandoned remote branches.

payload.chose: `sofar list` and `sofar status` fold the UNION of every copy of a log by default. The copies are this checkout's file, every other worktree's working file (uncommitted appends included, read as files with no subprocess), and every local branch NOT merged into HEAD and not checked out anywhere, read at its tip through one `git cat-file --batch`. Duplicate ids are dropped and this checkout's lines stay first, so their line numbers and warnings are unchanged. Output names where the extra events live and what this checkout alone holds. It renders nothing extra, byte-identical to before, when no other copy adds an event. `--here` restores the single-copy view. Remote-tracking refs are opt-in with `--remotes` (operator said "do it" without ruling on remotes, so the conservative default stands).
payload.over: (a) Remote-tracking refs on by default. (b) Reading every branch, merged ones included. (c) Moving the record off-branch, or writing events through to main's copy (rejected in note 01M31PRW). (d) Leaving the default local and adding the union as an opt-in flag.

## Record copies across branches
The record is committed, so every branch carries its own copy of every
events.jsonl, and a checkout that folds only its own copy reports whatever
that branch last saw. Measured 2026-09-21: memory-lead's copies held 11, 143,
132 and 149 of 158 events. No single copy was right, including the branch
that did the work. `sofar status` and `sofar list` therefore fold the UNION
of every copy they can see (branch-visibility D1). This is read-side only: it
never writes to any copy and adds no event type.

**Why the union is well defined.** The fold replays in ulid order and is
convergent (§Cursor primitive (sync-ready contract)), and duplicate ids are
dropped before it runs. The union's state is therefore exactly what merging
every branch with `merge=union` would produce.

**Which copies** (`core/record-copies.ts`):
- Every OTHER worktree of the repo, read as its working file, so uncommitted
  appends count. They are found from the common git dir's own files
  (`<common>/worktrees/*/gitdir`, plus the main checkout when the common dir
  is `<root>/.git`), with no subprocess. A worktree whose directory is gone
  is skipped.
- Every local branch that is NOT merged into HEAD and NOT checked out in a
  worktree, read at its tip. This costs one `git for-each-ref --no-merged=HEAD`
  and at most two `git cat-file --batch` processes (the initiatives tree, then
  the logs). A merged branch is skipped with no loss: logs are append-only and
  merge=union, so its whole committed log is already in HEAD's. A checked-out
  branch is covered by its worktree's file. A ref at the same commit as one
  already taken adds nothing and is dropped.
- Remote-tracking refs only with `--remotes` (D1: opt-in). They cover
  teammates' pushed branches but also bring in abandoned ones. A teammate's
  unpushed work on another machine is invisible to any local read; that case
  belongs to §Sync client (v2 — api.sofar.sh, the D14 seam; sync-client, Jul 2026).
- Never this checkout: its file is "here" and is read as it always was. Any
  failure (no git, an unborn HEAD, an unreadable checkout) degrades to fewer
  copies, never to an error.

**The union fold.** This checkout's lines come first and verbatim, so the
line numbers and warnings for them are exactly those of a single-copy fold.
Each other copy then adds only lines whose id is new to the union. A line
with no readable id is left out, since the fold would skip it anyway. A copy
that is a byte prefix of this checkout's log (a branch that forked and never
wrote to this record) is skipped without a line walk. Warnings about added
lines name the copy and that copy's own line number (`r1-fixes line 190:
unknown event type …`): another branch may run a newer engine.

**What is rendered.** When another copy adds at least one event, the headline
progress is the union's, and the output says what it is made of: this
checkout's own figure (or "not on this checkout") and each contributing copy
with the number of events it holds that this checkout lacks, most first.
Plain `sofar status` adds an `Across branches:` block under `Progress:`. The
styled view adds an `⚠ Across branches` block under the goal. `sofar list`
adds an `across branches: here D/T tasks done, +N event(s) on <copy>, <copy>,
+K more` part to the entry. A task done on a branch has not shipped to this
one, and an abandoned branch must never read as landed work, so a merged
number is never shown alone. When no other copy adds an event, both commands
print byte-identically to a single-copy fold. `--here` restores the
single-copy view.

**Scope.** Only `sofar status` (one shot) and `sofar list`. `status --watch`,
`sofar next`, get_state and every hook still read this checkout alone
(branch-visibility 3.1–3.3). Reading N checkouts is operator-command cost
(about 95 ms on this repo's 5 worktrees and 62 initiatives), not hot-path
cost. Writes always land in this checkout's copy: never write to, or
rewrite, another checkout's copy (D1).

## Sync client (v2 — api.sofar.sh, the D14 seam; sync-client, Jul 2026)"""
